title: Is binge-watching the new addiction
titleChinese: 连续“刷剧”成为现代人新瘾
paragraphs: Have you ever loved a TV show? I mean really loved it? Like, you can't wait to get to work to talk about it loved it? What about the cliffhanger? That‘s the unresolved situation at the end of the episode which makes you want to watch the next one. But, when will the next one be?

In the past, viewers had to wait up to a week for the next episode of their favourite shows. What agony! But, that's not the case any more. And hand in hand with that comes a, possibly dangerous, growing social trend. We speak of binge-watching.

Binge-watching is when a person watches more than one episode of a show in quick succession. With developments in the speed and connectivity of the internet, increases in technology and the rise of on-demand entertainment companies, people can now have their favourite shows streamed directly to their television at their convenience.

This behaviour is nothing new. In fact, 'binge-watching' has been officially listed in dictionaries since 2015. The entertainment companies recognise this behaviour and many take steps to encourage it. Often, instead of releasing each episode on a week-by-week basis, an entire series will become available concurrently. Once the episode finishes, many platforms will display pop-ups with 'you might like' suggestions, or will automatically play the next episode.

However, this wondrous gift may in fact be a poisoned chalice. Recent research from British media watchdog Ofcom suggests that this behaviour may have become a hindrance. Out of the more than half of British adults who watch more than one episode of a show back-to-back, almost a third have admitted missing sleep or becoming tired as a result; and one quarter have neglected their household chores. Next we'll be missing work! Bingeing has other connections — binge eating, binge drinking and binge smoking. All of which are often associated with compulsive behaviour, a lack of control and a possible route to addiction. Lindsey Fussell, consumer group director at Ofcom, said: "The days of waiting a week for the next episode are largely gone, with people finding it hard to resist watching multiple episodes around the house or on the move." If people find binge-watching hard to resist, coupled with the fact that it has shown to lead to negligence in many, are we witnessing the birth of a new type of addiction?

The myriad of information and entertainment that television and online media can bring us is, many would say, a good thing. It offers us opportunities to better understand the world we live in, educate ourselves and enjoy much needed downtime. However, like any behaviour done to excess, it can become dangerous. And when the activity begins to bleed into other areas, causing us to stop functioning — then it becomes a problem. So, what's the answer? Moderation! Neither a tiny amount, nor too much. After all, as the old proverb says... a little of what you fancy does you good.

vocabulary.entry: cliffhanger [n.] /ˈklɪfhæŋə/ 扣人心弦的悬念 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The episode ended with a cliffhanger that left everyone eager for the next one.
vocabulary.translation: 这一集以一个扣人心弦的悬念结束，让每个人都迫不及待想看下一集。

vocabulary.entry: agony [n.] /ˈæɡəni/ 极度痛苦；苦恼 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Waiting for the results was pure agony.
vocabulary.translation: 等待结果纯粹是一种痛苦。

vocabulary.entry: binge-watching [n.] /ˈbɪndʒ wɒtʃɪŋ/ 疯狂追剧 (新词；口语)
vocabulary.example: Binge-watching has become a popular way to consume TV shows.
vocabulary.translation: 疯狂追剧已成为观看电视剧的流行方式。

vocabulary.entry: succession [n.] /səkˈseʃən/ 连续；接连 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He won the championship for the third year in succession.
vocabulary.translation: 他连续第三年赢得了冠军。

vocabulary.entry: concurrently [adv.] /kənˈkʌrəntli/ 同时地 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The two movies were released concurrently in cinemas.
vocabulary.translation: 这两部电影同时在影院上映。

vocabulary.entry: pop-ups [n. pl.] /ˈpɒp ʌps/ 弹出窗口 (口语；单数: pop-up)
vocabulary.example: Pop-ups can be annoying when you‘re browsing the web.
vocabulary.translation: 浏览网页时弹出窗口可能很烦人。

vocabulary.entry: poisoned chalice [n.] /ˌpɔɪzənd ˈtʃælɪs/ 看似诱人实则有害的事物 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The promotion turned out to be a poisoned chalice, with too much stress and responsibility.
vocabulary.translation: 这次晋升结果成了烫手山芋，压力和责任太大。

vocabulary.entry: hindrance [n.] /ˈhɪndrəns/ 阻碍；障碍 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: His lack of experience was a hindrance to his career.
vocabulary.translation: 他缺乏经验对他的事业是一个障碍。

vocabulary.entry: resist [v.] /rɪˈzɪst/ 抵制；抗拒
vocabulary.example: She couldn‘t resist the temptation to check her phone.
vocabulary.translation: 她无法抗拒查看手机的诱惑。

vocabulary.entry: myriad [n.] /ˈmɪriəd/ 无数；大量 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: There are a myriad of reasons to learn a new language.
vocabulary.translation: 学习一门新语言有无数的理由。

vocabulary.entry: bleed into [phr.] /bliːd ˈɪntə/ 渗透到；蔓延到
vocabulary.example: Work stress often bleeds into personal life.
vocabulary.translation: 工作压力常常渗透到个人生活中。

vocabulary.entry: negligence [n.] /ˈneɡlɪdʒəns/ 疏忽；粗心大意 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The accident was caused by the driver’s negligence.
vocabulary.translation: 事故是由司机的疏忽造成的。

vocabulary.entry: compulsive [adj.] /kəmˈpʌlsɪv/ 强迫性的；难以控制的 (心理学词汇)
vocabulary.example: He has a compulsive need to check his phone every few minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 他每隔几分钟就有强迫性地查看手机的需要。

vocabulary.entry: addiction [n.] /əˈdɪkʃən/ 成瘾；上瘾 (心理学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Drug addiction is a serious health problem.
vocabulary.translation: 毒瘾是一个严重的健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: downtime [n.] /ˈdaʊntaɪm/ 休息时间；停机时间 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Everyone needs some downtime to relax.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都需要一些休息时间来放松。

vocabulary.entry: moderation [n.] /ˌmɒdəˈreɪʃən/ 适度；节制 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Alcohol should be consumed in moderation.
vocabulary.translation: 饮酒应当适量。

vocabulary.entry: watchdog [n.] /ˈwɒtʃdɒɡ/ 监察机构；监督者
vocabulary.example: The media watchdog monitors the content of news broadcasts.
vocabulary.translation: 媒体监察机构监督新闻广播的内容。

vocabulary.entry: back-to-back [adj.] /ˌbæk tə ˈbæk/ 连续的；一个接一个的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: They played two games back-to-back.
vocabulary.translation: 他们连续打了两场比赛。

vocabulary.entry: neglect [v.] /nɪˈɡlekt/ 忽视；忽略 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He neglected his studies and failed the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 他忽视了学习，结果考试不及格。

vocabulary.entry: fancy [v.] /ˈfænsi/ 想要；喜欢 (英式口语)
vocabulary.example: Do you fancy going to the cinema tonight?
vocabulary.translation: 你今晚想去看电影吗？

sentences.chinese: 与此同时，一种可能危险的、日益增长的社会趋势也随之而来。

sentences.chinese: 疯狂追剧指的是一个人接连不断地观看一部电视剧的多集内容。

sentences.chinese: 这种行为并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.chinese: 事实上，“疯狂追剧”自2015年起就已被正式收录进词典。

sentences.chinese: 娱乐公司认识到了这种行为，并且很多公司都采取措施来鼓励它。

sentences.chinese: 通常，一整部电视剧会同时上线，而不是每周播出一集。

sentences.chinese: 一集结束后，许多平台会显示带有“你可能喜欢”推荐内容的弹出窗口，或者会自动播放下一集。

sentences.english: However, this wondrous gift may in fact be a poisoned chalice.
sentences.chinese: 然而，这份奇妙的礼物实际上可能是一个看似诱人实则有害的事物。

sentences.chinese: 英国媒体监管机构英国通信管理局最近的研究表明，这种行为可能已经成为了一种阻碍。

sentences.english: Out of the more than half of British adults who watch more than one episode of a show back-to-back, almost a third have admitted missing sleep or becoming tired as a result; and one quarter have neglected their household chores.
sentences.chinese: 在超过一半连续观看多集电视剧的英国成年人中，几乎三分之一的人承认因此而睡眠不足或感到疲惫；四分之一的人忽视了他们的家务。

sentences.chinese: 接下来我们可能连工作都要耽误了！

sentences.chinese: 疯狂追剧还与其他行为有关——暴饮暴食、酗酒和大量吸烟。

sentences.chinese: 所有这些行为通常都与强迫性行为、缺乏自控力以及可能导致成瘾相关。

sentences.chinese: 英国通信管理局的消费者团体主管林赛·富塞尔说：“等上一周看下一集的日子在很大程度上已经一去不复返了，人们发现无论是在家里还是在外出途中，都很难抗拒连续观看多集电视剧。”

sentences.chinese: 许多人会说，电视和网络媒体能够带给我们的海量的信息和娱乐是一件好事。

sentences.chinese: 它为我们提供了更好地了解我们所生活的世界、自我教育以及享受非常需要的休闲时光的机会。

sentences.english: However, like any behaviour done to excess, it can become dangerous.
sentences.chinese: 然而，就像任何过度的行为一样，它也可能变得危险。

sentences.english: And when the activity begins to bleed into other areas, causing us to stop functioning — then it becomes a problem.
sentences.chinese: 当这种行为开始渗透到其他领域，导致我们无法正常生活时——那么它就成了一个问题。

sentences.english: So, what's the answer?
sentences.chinese: 那么，解决办法是什么呢？

sentences.english: Moderation!
sentences.chinese: 适度！

sentences.english: Neither a tiny amount, nor too much.
sentences.chinese: 既不要太少，也不要太多。

sentences.english: After all, as the old proverb says... a little of what you fancy does you good.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，正如那句古老的谚语所说......喜欢的东西，稍微享受一点对你有好处。
